# ARC edge-block diagonal packing

For the observed Continual-ARC task family (seen as task `task-4185d0e5`), the input contains four monochrome components near the bottom and/or side edges. The output moves them into a contiguous diagonal chain starting at the upper-left.

## Procedure
1. Identify the four connected monochrome components and record each exact shape (including dimensions), color, and original left-to-right order along the bottom edge / continuation up the right edge. In the examples, the rightmost component is a vertical bar on the right edge.
2. Preserve component shapes and color identities; do not rotate them.
3. Pack the components in the same order into a down-right staircase, beginning at the upper-left. Each succeeding component starts farther down and right, joining the previous one at the diagonal contact/overlap. When shapes overlap at the join, the later component's color takes precedence (as seen in the demonstrated output).
4. Keep all other cells zero and retain the original grid dimensions.
5. Check the constructed output against the example geometry: in the demo, 2x2 blocks and a 1x4 vertical bar became a staircase from the upper-left, with the next block offset down-right and the final vertical bar on the lower-right end. For fresh instances, use the input component dimensions to set offsets so the pieces connect as a single chain; don't copy offsets blindly.

## Caution
This rule is inferred from limited demonstrations. Verify component count, order, shapes, and connecting staircase against each new input before submitting. The demonstrated example confirms components may overwrite cells at their joining edge, so resolve the seam in favor of the later block.",
